beats.title: Make them collinear
beats.instruction: Drag point C until all three points (A, B, C) lie on the same line.
beats.successMessage: Nice — A, B, C are now collinear.

steps.text: Identify the line. Notation DE with both-way arrows means an infinite line through D and E.
Check whether F lies anywhere on that infinite line, not only between D and E.
F is visibly off the line, so F is not on line DE and the three points are not collinear.

items.prompt: Which notation refers to a LINE through points P and Q?
choices: PQ with a single right arrow
items.explanation: Two-way arrows mean the line extends forever in both directions.

choices: they all lie on the same line
they all lie in the same plane
items.explanation: Collinear literally means 'on a common line.'

items.prompt: How many lines pass through any two distinct points?
hints: Think about laying a ruler across two dots.
Try drawing a second straight line through both dots — can you?
Postulate: through any two points there is exactly one line.

items.prompt: How many planes pass through any three non-collinear points?
hints: Think of a three-legged stool — it always rests flat.
Could you tilt the plane and still pass through all three?
Three non-collinear points fix exactly one plane.

items.prompt: If two distinct planes intersect, the intersection is…
hints: Picture two pages of an open book.
Where do the two pages meet?
The intersection of two distinct planes is a line — the spine of the book.

items.prompt: Points P, Q, R lie on line m. Are P, Q, R collinear? Answer yes or no.
hints: All three points lie on line m, so…
Yes — three points on a single line are collinear by definition.

testItems.prompt: Points X and Y are given. How many distinct lines pass through both?
Which symbol denotes a line through points A and B?

choices: Two intersecting lines determine a plane.
testItems.explanation: Three points are not automatically on a single line. Three non-collinear points form a triangle, not a line.

testItems.prompt: Why are 'point,' 'line,' and 'plane' called undefined terms?
choices: Because mathematicians forgot to define them.
Because they are described rather than formally defined, to avoid circular definitions.
Because their definitions are kept secret.
Because they are not actually used in geometry.

testItems.prompt: A line contains points R, S, T in that order. Name two different ways to denote this same line.
testItems.answer: line RS and line RT (or any pair of the three letters)
testItems.rubric: Accept any two distinct two-point notations for the line.

testItems.prompt: Plane M contains points P and Q. According to the postulates, what else must be true?
choices: Plane M contains only P and Q.
Line PQ lies entirely in plane M.
Plane M contains no other lines.
Plane M is parallel to line PQ.
testItems.explanation: Postulate: if two points lie in a plane, the entire line through them lies in that plane.
